record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: Let MS be the modal language for distance models whose terms are built from predicate letters, nominals interpreted as singleton locations, Boolean negation, set difference, and distance modalities. In the fragment using only the operators exists<=a tau and exists>a tau, the formula exists<=a tau holds at a point x when some point satisfying tau is at distance at most a from x, and exists>a tau holds at x when some point satisfying tau is at distance greater than a from x, where a is a nonnegative rational parameter. Over metric models, where the distance function satisfies identity of indiscernibles, symmetry, and the triangle inequality, what is the computational complexity of deciding satisfiability for this fragment when the numerical parameters are encoded in binary?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a modal language MS interpreted over metric models. A metric model is a pair $(M,\nu)$ where $M=(W,d)$ is a metric space — that is, $W$ is a nonempty set and $d:W\times W\to\mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0}$ satisfies (i) $d(x,y)=0$ iff $x=y$, (ii) $d(x,y)=d(y,x)$, and (iii) $d(x,z)\leq d(x,y)+d(y,z)$ — and $\nu$ assigns to each predicate letter a subset of $W$ and to each nominal a singleton subset of $W$. Formulas (terms) of MS are built from predicate letters and nominals using Boolean negation, set difference, and distance modalities. In the fragment under consideration, only the following two distance modalities are allowed, with parameter $a\in\mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0}$:
\[\exists^{\leq a}\tau, \qquad \exists^{> a}\tau.\]
Semantics: $x\models \exists^{\leq a}\tau$ iff there exists $y\in W$ with $d(x,y)\leq a$ and $y\models\tau$; $x\models \exists^{> a}\tau$ iff there exists $y\in W$ with $d(x,y)>a$ and $y\models\tau$. A formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable in this class if there is a metric model and a point $x$ such that $x\models\varphi$.

Determine the exact computational complexity of the satisfiability problem for formulas of this fragment over metric models, under the convention that all rational numerical parameters $a$ occurring in the input formula are encoded in binary.
artifact.status_search_result: Known related results establish PSpace-hardness under binary coding for related distance-modality fragments and ExpTime-completeness for richer languages, while unary coding yields NP. No definitive published resolution of the exact complexity of the specific $\exists^{\leq a},\exists^{>a}$ fragment with binary-encoded rationals over metric spaces was located.

status_evidence.title: Logics of metric spaces (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Without qualitative temporal operators the complexity depends on whether binary or unary coding of parameters is assumed: it is still PSpace-hard under binary coding but in NP under unary coding.
status_evidence.claim: Binary-coding satisfiability for distance-modality fragments is known PSpace-hard, but a matching upper bound for this specific fragment was not located.

status_evidence.title: Modal Logics for Metric Spaces: Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems list on modal logics interpreted over metric spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem with no resolution indicated in subsequent surveys located.
